cards.subject: a bright Playful Curves bedroom for a child aged 2 to 5, with a flower-shaped craft table and a stack of round bouclé poufs
cards.scene: A calm airy room with a pale ash floor and cream walls. A scalloped felt rug in deep eucalyptus green holds wax crayons in a wooden cup and an open drawing book, with one small wooden arch block beside them. On the LEFT side wall, away from the mural: a flower-shaped craft table 45 cm high in pale lacquered birch, with a stack of two round bouclé poufs in warm ochre and barberry red beside it, and a small arch-shaped framed picture above. Crisp morning daylight from a window on the LEFT lies in clear patches on the floor. At the right edge of the frame an open white door leads into the room; a toddler girl of about two and a half in a sunny ochre knit sweater and cream trousers has just come through it and stands two steps inside the room at the right edge of the frame with her back to the camera, in mid-stride with both arms swinging out to the sides, her face turned away from the camera so no facial detail is visible, well away from the mural. Palette: pale birch, warm ochre, barberry red, cream and white.
cards.framing: Shot from the right part of the room at eye level, turned about 25 degrees toward the mural wall, so the LEFT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the big pink and yellow cosmos flowers of the meadow and the butterflies above them: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale.

cards.subject: a warm Fun Haus bedroom for a child aged 6 to 10, with a curved birch study desk and a low striped single bed
cards.scene: A sunny tidy room with a dark walnut herringbone floor. A flat-weave rug in sand and brick red lies on the floor, with a classic globe on a turned solid wood stand beside the bed. On the RIGHT side wall, away from the mural: a curved birch study desk 75 cm high with an open book ledge, illustrated books, wooden pencil cups and an ergonomic wooden chair, beside a single bed 90 by 200 cm in a low frame with caramel-and-cream striped bedding and one blue cushion, and a small framed vintage circus picture above the desk. Warm morning sunbeams from a window on the RIGHT lie in soft patches on the floor. A sheer cream linen curtain hangs at the extreme left edge of the frame, close to the camera and slightly out of focus, as a foreground layer. Palette: caramel, brick red, cream, saturated blue and walnut brown and.
cards.framing: Shot from the left part of the room at natural eye level, turned about 30 degrees toward the mural wall, so the RIGHT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the big pink and yellow cosmos flowers of the meadow and the butterflies above them: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale. Nothing stands in front of the mural.

clips.motion: The camera stays completely still on a tripod and does not move at all. A toddler girl of about two and a half in a sunny ochre knit sweater and cream trousers, standing just inside the open doorway at the right edge of the frame with her back to the camera, runs a few quick happy steps across the floor toward the mural wall and stops about two metres in front of it; on the last step both arms rise high above her head in delight and she stands still. Her face is never visible to the camera, not even in profile: only the back of her head, her hair and her clothes are seen. The white door stays exactly as it is, open. The rug, the toys and the room stay exactly as they are. The light stays constant.

clips.motion: A smooth slow first-person walk-in: the camera advances steadily straight forward into the room at natural eye level, as if a person is slowly entering, with no sideways drift, no tilt and no rotation. The sheer cream curtain in the extreme foreground on the left leaves the frame as the camera advances past it, and the nearer objects shift more than the farther ones, giving a natural depth parallax.
